newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise to new highs, boosted by dollar.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise to new highs, boosted by dollar.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Tuesday, lifting the blue-chip CAC-40 index to new highs, in an advance propelled by gains in the dollar and bond futures.
"The market's very firm with the support of the dollar, which has had an equally positive impact on the bond markets," a trader said.
The CAC-40 index was up 19.59 points, or 0.74 percent, at 2,654.07 at 0930 GMT, after hitting an all time high of 2,656.90 in early trading. Resistance on the CAC is seen at 2,675.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up 19.5 points at 2,661.5.
Shares in steelmaker Usinor jumped 4.02 percent to 87.90 francs despite a big fall in 1996 profit which was nonetheless better than some analysts had expected.

Usinor said on Tuesday that net attributable profit fell to 1.49 billion francs from a record 4.43 billion and cut its dividend to three francs per share from four. Many market operators had expected the dividend to be halved.
Usinor said it hoped for better 1997 results based on signs of a pickup in demand but it said average prices would be lower.

Tyremaker Michelin's stock rebounded 2.02 percent, more than recouping Monday's fall after the company said it planned to redeem 3.5 billion francs of convertible bonds ahead of schedule in a move that will boost its capital and improve its debt-to-equity ratio.
